record.paper_title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis
record.context_brief: Recovering spacetime topology from interval domains
record.original_question: Can the topology of a spacetime be reconstructed in a rigorous technical way from the topology of an interval domain, as suggested by the equivalence between globally hyperbolic posets and interval domains? Relatedly, does the fact that candidate causal spacetime topologies such as the Zeeman fine topology, Göbel’s generalization, and the Hawking-King-McCarthy topology are non-metrizable reveal what kind of non-manifold topology should be regarded as the right topology for spacetime when the underlying model is order-theoretic?

evidence.quote: Question 3: In the light of Theorem 3.8, we ask whether the topology of a spacetime can be reconstructed, in some technical and rigorous way, from the topology of an interval domain.

The spacetime topologies that we have mentioned in this section, like for example the Zeeman fine topology or its generalization by Göbel, or the one by Hawking-King-McCarthy are not metrizable; does this give us any insight on the appropriate candidate for a spacetime topology (other than the manifold topology), given that interval domains are order-theoretic objects?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A partially ordered set $(P,\le)$ is called bicontinuous if there is a way-below relation $\ll$ on $P$ such that for every $x\in P$ the sets $\{y:y\ll x\}$ and $\{y:x\ll y\}$ are directed/filtered with suprema/infima equal to $x$, and $a\ll b$ iff for every directed (resp. filtered) set with supremum (resp. infimum) $b$ (resp. $a$) the element $a$ (resp. $b$) is eventually below (resp. above) some member. The interval topology on $P$ is generated by the subbasis $\{y:a\ll y\}\cup\{y:y\ll b\}$ for $a,b\in P$. An interval domain is a continuous dcpo whose elements are pairs $[a,b]$ with $a\le b$ in some bicontinuous poset, ordered by reverse inclusion.

A globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ is a time-oriented Lorentzian manifold whose causal relation $\le$ makes $(M,\le)$ a bicontinuous poset for which the interval topology coincides with the manifold topology, and the category of such spacetimes (with suitable order-preserving maps) is equivalent to a category of interval domains.

Several candidate "causal" topologies on a spacetime $M$ have been proposed in place of the manifold topology, including:
(i) the Zeeman fine topology, the finest topology on Minkowski space inducing the Euclidean topology on every timelike line and every spacelike hyperplane;
(ii) Göbel's generalization of the Zeeman topology to arbitrary Lorentzian manifolds;
(iii) the Hawking–King–McCarthy path topology, the finest topology on $M$ inducing the manifold topology on every timelike curve.
Each of these topologies is non-metrizable.

Problem. 
(a) Given only the interval domain $\mathbf{I} M$ associated to a globally hyperbolic spacetime $(M,g)$ (viewed as an abstract topological/order-theoretic object), give a rigorous procedure to reconstruct a topology on the underlying point set $M$ (identified with the maximal elements of $\mathbf{I} M$) and identify it with a naturally defined spacetime topology.
(b) Using the order-theoretic nature of interval domains, determine which non-manifold, non-metrizable topology on $M$ (such as the Zeeman, Göbel, or Hawking–King–McCarthy topology, or another order-theoretically defined topology) is canonically singled out by this reconstruction, and explain in what sense it is the "right" topology for spacetime in the order-theoretic framework.
artifact.category_tag: Causal structure and domain theory of spacetimes
artifact.status_search_result: Martin and Panangaden (Comm. Math. Phys., 2006) showed that a globally hyperbolic spacetime can be order-theoretically reconstructed as a bicontinuous poset whose interval topology equals the manifold topology, and that the category of globally hyperbolic posets is equivalent to a category of interval domains. This addresses part (a) by yielding the manifold topology from the interval domain. However, whether order-theoretic considerations single out a specific non-metrizable causal topology (such as Zeeman, Göbel, or Hawking–King–McCarthy) as the canonical "right" spacetime topology in this framework does not appear to be resolved in the literature; no definitive resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: A Domain of Spacetime Intervals in General Relativity
status_evidence.snippet: A globally hyperbolic spacetime with its causality relation is a bicontinuous poset whose interval topology is the manifold topology... the category of globally hyperbolic posets is equivalent to a special category of domains called interval domains.
status_evidence.claim: The manifold topology of a globally hyperbolic spacetime is recovered as the interval topology of an associated bicontinuous poset / interval domain.

status_evidence.title: Globally Hyperbolic Spacetimes as Posets
status_evidence.snippet: Globally hyperbolic spacetimes viewed as posets and their relation to interval domains.
status_evidence.claim: The order-theoretic reconstruction of globally hyperbolic spacetimes via interval domains is an active research topic.
